title: [Physics] Inconsistent behavior of Area2D detection states, especially when overlapping
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.7stable, 4.6.3stable, 4.3stable - Partially reproducible in: 3.6.2stable (the difference is that in 3.6.2, even if you modify the layer/mask while the areas are already overlapping, the Area2D cannot detect it) ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12490F (12 threads) - 31.81 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description **Note:** I am using translation tools and AI assistance to describe this issue, as my English is not very good. I apologize in advance for any inaccuracies in the title or description. As this issue may encompass multiple problems, and I am uncertain whether they should be reported separately, I have combined them here. **Scenario:** I have a detection Area2D (like an enemy sensor). An enemy is already overlapping with it. At runtime, I need to change the detection state for that particular enemy – turning detection on or off for that enemy only. The following diagram illustrates this scenario: I can think of at least four ways (modifying in the Inspector) to change the detection state between two Area2Ds, but in practice, the behavior is inconsistent. - Disable detecter `monitoring` (it works) - Disable target `monitorable` (not work, bug?) - Modify detecter `collision_mask` value (it works) - Modify target `collision_layer` value (it works) **Additionally:** attempts to modify the target `monitoring` resulted in unexpected behavior (this causes the target Area2D to trigger one area_exited and one area_entered event). I am not sure why this happens, but it appears to be unintended behavior. Also, when changing this value via code (not in the Inspector), the abnormal behavior only appears if the change is made in _process() or _input(); doing it in _physics_process() works fine. **Sub‑issue:** When the target is moved, and its monitorable property is turned on before entering the detection area, and then turned off during overlap/entry, the exit signal is still fired upon leaving – this is not expected. In contrast, if monitorable is disabled before the target ever enters the detection area, neither entry nor exit signals are emitted, which behaves as expected. **Overall, it seems that modifications to `monitorable` have no effect while the areas are already overlapping.** **Demonstration video:** 0.
